next_action.description: FIX THE ENHANCE DEAD-BOX FIRST - it is root-caused, do not re-investigate. The enhancer is INNOCENT: the op runs, onText fires, _fieldValues[d.to] receives the text. `_writeFieldValue` (MpiBaseFlow.js:763) does `qs('.mpi-base-flow__field-text', wrap)` then `inp.value = text`, but `.mpi-base-flow__field-text` is the MOUNT HOST DIV (declaredFields.js:340), not the textarea MpiInput renders inside it. Assigning `.value` on a div sets an expando: no error, no log, no repaint, clean exit. Every symptom falls out of that one line - the box stays empty, the ENHANCE button correctly goes GREY (because _paintEnhance's `stale` reads _fieldValues, which IS filled - the grey button was evidence of SUCCESS and read as failure), reopening/reusing the flow shows the text, and clear-on-edit is broken the same way. DO NOT just widen the selector to `.mpi-base-flow__field-text textarea` - writing textarea.value behind MpiInput's back desyncs the Primitive. Reach the component API: check what MpiInput exposes, and change `_liveFields` (it stores the wrapper element today) to keep the instance or expose setValue on the mounted el. Guard it with a real-pixel probe asserting the TEXTAREA's rendered value after a programmatic write - never that _fieldValues holds it, because the state was right the whole time; tests/ cannot see the DOM so this is a desktop spec or a documented playwright probe. THEN the two UI asks, both approved by Fabio and neither built: (1) toggles become icon+label MpiButtons - change the `toggle` type itself in declaredFields.js, icon optional, suppress the top label the way `button` already is at line 148; (2) a LoRA button that opens a LoRA panel, plus a new route for flow LoRAs - the graph already carries Input_Lora_1..6 and comfyController already routes them, what is missing is entirely UI (declaredFields.js has NO lora type and NO shipped Flow declares a rack - plan.md's older claim that ltx-extend and foley ship one is WRONG and is corrected). Ask Fabio how many slots show by default and whether each exposes strength_model. THEN /mpi-flow-graphics.

key_decisions: THE FLUX RATIO ROWS ARE DECLINED ON EVIDENCE, NOT PREFERENCE. Do not re-propose 'fixing' the nominal labels. Eight of the nine values are exact SDXL training buckets and the labels were fitted to them afterwards; every truthful replacement leaves the bucket set, and 1280x720 is not even /32 which BFL's FLUX API requires. The 8:5 pair keeps 1280x800. What the investigation does NOT establish: the buckets are SDXL's and this table feeds flux/chroma/klein/krea2, none of them SDXL - nobody has measured whether a bucket value beats a non-bucket one on any of the four. Both sides rest on an unmeasured assumption; the pixels simply have the better provenance.

THE SWITCH BANK IS THE ANSWER TO 'ONE FIELD, N GRAPH VALUES' AND MPI-586 MUST REUSE IT, not invent a second. That is why the banks carry any_1..any_5 rather than a boolean. Portable record: docs/playbooks/add-flow/ui/switch-bank-fields.md.

CONSTANTS BEHIND A SWITCH GET NON-`Input_` TITLES. In this codebase `Input_*` means 'the app may inject this', and a constant that only takes effect on one arm is a trap - injecting it succeeds, changes nothing on the other arms, and reports nothing. That is why 676/677 were retitled W_1k/H_1k. Free here because smoke-workflows.mjs never executes a flow_*.json (its own comment, line 1068).

A MISSING SWITCH SELECTOR IS THE WORST SILENT SKIP - it does not break the graph, it pins every run to any_1 while the control still renders and the run still succeeds. input_quality is pinned in tests/inject-params-titles.test.cjs for exactly that.
